prompt:
A car of mass $1200\ \text{kg}$ accelerates from rest to $15\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ in $6.0\ \text{s}$.

**(a)** Calculate the average acceleration of the car. **[1]**

**(b)** Calculate the average resultant force on the car. **[1]**

**(c)** The driving force on the car is larger than your answer to (b). Explain why. **[1]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $a = \tfrac{15}{6.0} = 2.5\ \text{m s}^{-2}$ ✓

**(b)** $F = ma = 1200 \times 2.5 = 3.0 \times 10^3\ \text{N}$ ✓

**(c)** Resistive forces (air resistance, friction) act against the motion, so the driving force must exceed the resultant force by their size ✓

prompt: A force of 40 N acts on a 2.0 kg trolley at rest for 0.50 s. What is the final speed of the trolley?
markscheme: **B.** Impulse $= 40\times0.50 = 20$ N s $= \Delta p$; $v = 20/2.0 = 10$ m s⁻¹.

prompt:
A 1.2 kg cart moving at 3.0 m s⁻¹ collides with a stationary 0.80 kg cart. They stick together.

**(a)** Calculate their common velocity. **[2]**

**(b)** Calculate the kinetic energy lost. **[2]**

**(c)** State, with a reason, whether the collision is elastic. **[2]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $1.2\times3.0 = 2.0v$ ✓; $v = 1.8$ m s⁻¹ ✓

**(b)** Initial $E_k = 5.4$ J, final $= 3.24$ J ✓; lost $= 2.16 \approx 2.2$ J ✓

**(c)** Inelastic ✓, because kinetic energy is not conserved ✓
